text:
maya: ran an nsys trace of the kvcache-prefetch path, seeing repeated H2D memcpy chunks on stream 3 that appear to overlap kernels on stream 1, but the CPU thread that submits prefetches shows multi-100ms sleeps between submissions. wondering if stream assignment or host-copy mode is causing blocking.

jon: can you paste the nsys command + a tiny text dump of the timeline ranges? also which driver/OS?

maya: ran: `nsys profile -o trace_prefetch --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt ./inference_srv --profile-prefetch`
snippet from timeline view (condensed):
```
H2D memcpy (stream 3): 0.002s - 0.007s
Kernel K1 (stream 1): 0.003s - 0.010s
CPU prefetch thread sleep: 0.007s - 0.110s
H2D memcpy (stream 3): 0.112s - 0.117s
Kernel K2 (stream 1): 0.113s - 0.121s
```

maya: NVTX ranges show `[nvtx:prefetch]` wrapping memcpy calls. not a single-threaded stall pattern before this change.

lee: hypothesis: prefetch thread is using pageable buffers -> cudaMemcpyAsync may sync on CPU if driver falls back. or the submitter thread is getting preempted (cpu sleep) so submissions don't enqueue early enough to overlap. any signs of `cudaHostRegister`/pinned usage?

sam: we rolled the kernel-selection heuristic change in last week's deploy (selector picks stream 1 for compute and stream 3 for copies to reduce contention). could be we accidentally forced copies onto a stream that needs more CPU work to submit. might explain why moving copies to stream 1 previously gave better overlap.

jon: quick check: grep for `cudaHostAlloc`/`cudaHostRegister` in the prefetch code path. if absent, try a small repro that pins a buffer and issues `cudaMemcpyAsync` -> compare submission duration and observed overlap.

perf-bot: auto-summary for trace_prefetch: avg memcpy (H2D) = 5.1ms, avg kernel K = 8.7ms, avg CPU prefetch gap between submissions = 98ms, peak CPU sleep = 310ms. top CPU wakeups attributed to `prefetch_thread`.

maya: confirmed prefetch uses standard malloc buffers, not pinned. when I temporarily switched to pinned host buffers and kept stream assignment the same, observed memcpy latency drop and the CPU gaps shrank to ~4-8ms; overall tail latency improved ~18%.

lee: that strongly points to pageable fallback + CPU scheduling combo. two mitigation ideas: 1) switch prefetch to pinned allocations; 2) change batcher so copies are issued on the same stream as their target compute (stream affinity) to avoid cross-stream handshake costs.

sam: i'll revert the stream affinity heuristic change to the old policy in a canary and run the same nsys profile. also will add an experiment to give the prefetch thread SCHED_FIFO small RT prio to test preemption hypothesis.

jon: for the repro please also collect `perf sched` and a perfetto capture of kernel launch syscall wakeups — helps correlate the CPU sleeps to scheduler events.

maya: will attach the trace id once uploaded. also added a tiny microbenchmark that toggles `cudaHostAlloc` vs `malloc` for diff runs.

sam: thanks, nice find — low-effort fix might be pinning + revert heuristic until we vet stream assignment in more traces.

maya: 👍 i'll open a short PR that pins prefetch buffers and an A/B job in CI with nsys captures.
